channel.title: AI GridWatch — federal officials and candidates on data centers
channel.description: Every newly cited bill, letter, hearing question or statement on AI data centers by a sitting U.S. senator or a 2026 Senate or House candidate, with the source behind it. From AI GridWatch.

item.title: Tom Cotton (Republican, AR): Arkansas Advocate reported that Cotton, like his two challengers, said in an interview that he supports giving…
item.description: Arkansas Advocate reported that Cotton, like his two challengers, said in an interview that he supports giving Arkansans a vote on whether a data center is built near them, and that AI companies should be transparent about data centers' impacts on communities. This is the reporter's paraphrase of a September interview with 40/29 News; Cotton did not answer the Advocate's own questions. Source: https://www.newsfromthestates.com/article/issue-spotlight-what-candidates-arkansas-us-senate-race-say-about-ai-data-centers (Arkansas Advocate (via News From The States)). Kind: statement. Lean: mixed. Read 2026-11-28.

item.description: Said on Fox News' 'Sunday Morning Futures' that it should be up to the people of a community or a state to decide whether to host data centers, and that companies need to make their case, including that residents will not bear costs or environmental and health effects. Florida Politics summarised this as cities and counties deciding. Source: https://floridapolitics.com/archives/817705-ashley-moody-backs-local-control-on-data-center-question/ (Florida Politics).
